AddChannelMembersRequest.description: Who to add to a channel.

user_ids.description: Accounts to bring in. Anyone already in the channel is skipped rather than refused.

AddedMembersDto.description: Who was actually added, which is the request minus whoever was already there.

AdminUserDto.description: An account, as an administrator sees it while looking for the right one.

ApiHealth.description: Readiness payload returned by `/api/v1/health`, including dependency probes.

status.description: `"ok"` when every dependency is reachable, otherwise `"degraded"`.

version.description: Semantic version of the running binary.

ArchiveRequest.description: An archive an administrator points at, and the passphrase that opens it.

file.description: A name inside the server's import directory. Never a path: see [`resolve`].

passphrase.description: Absent for an archive that was never sealed, which only happens in development.

people.description:
What the administrator changed about the people after reading the plan: an address given to
somebody the export carried without one, an address corrected, a person left out.

Only the ones that changed. Everyone else arrives as the archive spells them.

oneOf.description:
Set to empty the instance before importing: every space and every account except the one
asking. Never a default, and refused unless the address matches and a backup less than a day
old has been recorded.

AttachmentDto.description: A file attached to a message.

deleted.description:
The file has since been removed from the space.

The attachment is still reported, because the message said something by carrying it and a
silent disappearance reads as a bug. What changes is that the client must not offer to open
bytes that are gone: every link to them answers 404, which is what a deleted attachment
looked like before this field existed.

AttachmentFolderDto.description: Where files dropped for an event of a calendar go.

AttendeeDto.description: One person on the list, and their answer for the series.

email.description: For someone invited by address only.

AttendeeInput.description: One person on the list, as the form sends it: an account, or an address (with a name to show).

Breadcrumb.description: One step of a folder breadcrumb, from the space root down to the current folder.

CalendarDto.description: A calendar as its viewer sees it.

default_reminders.description: The reminders a timed event gets by default, in minutes before it; empty is none.

hidden.description: Whether the viewer hid it from their view.

my_reminders.description:
The viewer's own reminders for the whole calendar: absent when they follow the defaults,
empty when they turned them off.

share_level.description:
For someone else's calendar shared with the caller: how far (`freebusy`, `read`, `write`),
and whose it is.

space_id.description: The space it belongs to; absent for a personal calendar.

CalendarMe.description: The viewer's own settings for a calendar; absent fields stay as they are.

reminder_default.description: `true` drops the viewer's own reminders and follows the calendar's defaults again.

reminders.description: The viewer's reminders for the calendar; empty for none.

CandidateDto.description: Someone a calendar may be shared with.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: Changing one's own password, knowing the current one.

ChangesDto.description: What changed in a space's conversations since a moment, for a client catching up.

messages.description:
The messages created, edited, deleted (as tombstones) or reacted to since then, replies
included, oldest first.

now.description:
The server's clock when the answer was computed: pass it as the next `since`. Taken before
the query, so a change made while it ran is sent again rather than skipped.

truncated.description: Too much changed, or too long ago, to be sent as a list: reload the space instead.

ChannelDto.description: The channel an event is linked to, as its viewer may know it.

accessible.description: Whether the viewer reads it (and may open it).

name.description: Absent for a private channel the viewer is not in.

ChannelInvitationRequest.description: Invite someone from outside into one group, as a guest who sees that group only.

ChannelMemberRoleDto.description:
A channel membership's role after a change.

Its own shape rather than the space one: the ladder is different (a channel has no guests) and so
is the audience, since a channel's roles are read by the people in it and by nobody else.

ChannelMembershipDto.description: A change to someone's place in a channel (see `RealtimeEnvelope::channel_membership`).

role.description: The new role, for a `role` change.

ChannelOrderRequest.description:
The order a space's administrators give its channels: the ones they can see, first to last.

Channels the caller cannot see (someone else's private channel) are not theirs to name and keep
their place among the others.

ChannelSummaryDto.description:
A channel's shared facts, pushed in real time when one is created or changed.

Deliberately not a [`ChannelDto`]: that shape carries per-caller state (favourite, membership,
unread count) which differs for every recipient, so a broadcast would hand one member's view to
everyone. Clients patch only the fields here and keep their own.

ChannelsReorderedDto.description:
Sent to a space's members when its channels were reordered. Carries only the space: each
client re-reads the list it may see, so no private channel is named to someone outside it.

CodeConfirm.description: Confirm an address with the code from the verification email.

code.description: Six digits; spaces and other separators are ignored.

ConversationPref.description: How much one conversation notifies one person.

ConversationRef.description: A reference to a just-created or fetched conversation.

default_reminders.description: Absent: ten minutes. Empty: no reminder.

write_access.description: `members` (the default) or `admins`; ignored for a personal calendar.

CreateChannelRequest.description: A new channel to create in a space.

allowed_roles.description:
Reserve the channel to these space roles. Absent or empty leaves it open to every role, and
the caller's own role has to be in the list: a room you are shut out of is not a room you
meant to make.

name.description: Display name; normalised to the lowercase, dash-separated form channels use.

type.description: `public` or `private`. A channel cannot be created already archived.

CreateDmRequest.description: Open (or fetch) a direct-message conversation with a set of users.

user_ids.description: The other participant(s); the caller is added implicitly.

calendar_id.description: The calendar to carry; `null` for all of them.

CreateFolderRequest.description: Create a folder inside a space (optionally under a parent folder).

CreateInvitationRequest.description: Create an invitation into a space.

email.description: Address to send it to. Omit for a shareable link.

expires_in_hours.description: Lifetime in hours. Defaults to 7 days, capped at 30.

max_uses.description: Maximum acceptances. Defaults to 1 for an addressed invitation, unlimited for a link.

CreateLinkRequest.description: What a new link should be.

expires_at.description: When it stops working, RFC 3339 (absent: never). Must be in the future.

password.description: The password it asks for (absent or blank: none).

CreateShareRequest.description: Create a share for a file. Exactly one target (user or channel) must be set.

CreateSpaceRequest.description: A new space to create. The caller becomes its owner.

name.description: Display name. The URL slug is derived from it and made unique.

CreatedFeedDto.description: A new subscription address: the only time its URL is given.

emailed.description:
Whether the invitation email actually went out. False when the invitation is a shareable
link (nothing to send) or when the relay refused it, in which case the `url` above is the
only way to deliver it.

url.description: Absolute link to hand to the invitee. Never retrievable again.

CreatedInvitationDto.description: The response to creating an invitation: the row, plus the link, shown exactly once.

DeleteCalendar.description: Deleting a calendar names it, as a confirmation.

Delivery.description:
How a new session reaches its holder.

A browser gets the id in the `__Host-` cookie, which its scripts cannot read. A native app has no
such jar it controls, so it receives the id itself, keeps it in the device's keychain and sends it
back as `Authorization: Bearer`. The session behind both is the same record, with the same limits.

DeviceRequest.description: A phone, as its app registers it.

token.description: The device token Apple or Google handed the app.

DirectMessageDto.description: A direct-message conversation in a space's sidebar list.

bot.description: Whether the sole counterpart is a bot account.

oneOf.description:
The latest message of the conversation, for the preview line of a conversation list.
Absent while nothing has been said.

muted.description: Whether the caller has muted this conversation.

name.description: Display label: the other participant, or a comma-joined list for a group.

notify_level.description: How much this conversation notifies the caller: `default`, `all`, `mentions` or `none`.

participant_ids.description:
Everyone in the conversation but the caller, in the order of `name`: a client draws a group's
faces from them and counts its people.

user_id.description:
The sole counterpart's user id for a 1:1 DM, so the client can overlay their live presence;
`None` for a group DM (no single counterpart to track).

DisableTotpRequest.description:
Turning off TOTP, which asks for the password: a session someone else has taken over must not
be able to strip the factor that would have stopped them.

attachments.description: Ids of already-uploaded files to add to the message. Existing attachments are preserved.

EditScope.description: Which part of a series a change or a deletion touches.

EditorDto.description: Someone editing a file in the office editor right now.

EmailRequest.description: A request that carries an email address (verification resend, reset request).

locale.description:
The language of the page the request came from: the message is written in it, since whoever
reads that page is who will read the message. Absent, the account's own language is used.

EmptiedDto.description: The answer to emptying the trash.

erased.description: How many trash entries were erased.

EventCardDto.description: An event as its card in a channel shows it to one reader.

my_status.description:
The reader's answer, when they are invited (`accepted` for the organiser of an event with
attendees).

organizer_id.description: Their account, so that the card does not ask them for an answer.

recurrence_id.description: That occurrence, for answering for one date.

start.description: Its next occurrence from now (its first, once it is over): RFC 3339 in UTC, or a date.

attendees.description: Who is invited, and their answer for the series.

oneOf.description: The channel it is linked to, as the viewer may know it.

my_own_reminders.description:
The viewer's own reminders for this event: absent when they follow their calendar's, empty
when they turned them off. What the details show as chosen.

oneOf.description: Its author, who organises it; absent once their account is gone.

EventDto.description: An event (or a series' head) with everything the form needs.

EventInput.description: An event as the form sends it, for a new event or a change.

attendees.description: The whole list of attendees (accounts or addresses), for the series; absent leaves it.

calendar_id.description: Another calendar to move the event to (whole-series changes only).

channel_id.description: The channel it is linked to: absent leaves it, `null` unlinks it.

end.description: Same form as `start`; exclusive for an all-day event (one day on the 7th ends on the 8th).

files.description: The whole list of the Drive files it carries; absent leaves it.

reminders.description: The author's own reminders for this event: absent leaves them, empty turns them off.

rrule.description: A bare RFC 5545 rule, `FREQ=...`; absent or null for a one-off event.

start.description: RFC 3339 for a timed event, `YYYY-MM-DD` for an all-day one.

tzid.description: IANA time zone of a timed event; the author's profile one when absent.

EventMe.description: The viewer's own reminder for one event (its whole series).

reminder_default.description: `true` drops the viewer's choice for this event and follows their calendar setting again.

reminders.description: The viewer's reminders for this event; empty for none.

FavoriteRequest.description: Pin a channel to the caller's favourites, or unpin it.

FeedDto.description: A subscription address, without its secret.

calendar_id.description: The calendar it carries; absent for the address that mixes them all.

last_used_at.description: RFC 3339; absent until a client first read it.

FileDto.description: A file or folder entry, with the current version's metadata folded in.

child_count.description:
How many entries a folder directly holds (removed ones and private conversations' files
left out). Absent for a file.

editors.description: Who is editing the file in the office editor right now (folder listings only).

has_thumbnail.description: Whether a thumbnail exists for this file's current version.

imported.description: Whether the file was migrated from another tool.

imported_source.description: The source connector a migrated file came from (e.g. "nextcloud"); absent for native files.

modified_by_id.description:
Who wrote the current version: the last person to change the file's contents, which is not
its owner once a colleague has uploaded or saved a version. Absent for a folder and for a
version with no known author (an import).

starred.description:
Whether the person asking keeps it among their favourites. Set by the listings that know who
asks; an event shared by a whole space leaves it out (false).

FileHitDto.description: A file matched by a search, enough to render a result row and open it.

FolderListing.description: The contents of a folder (or the space root when `folder_id` is `None`).

busy.description: The times they are taken, merged and in order.

exclude_event.description: An event to leave out: the one being moved, which should not stand in its own way.

HandoffCode.description: A single-use code handed between the web page and the app (two minutes).

Health.description:
Liveness payload returned by `/healthz`. This never touches dependencies, so it stays a pure
"the process is up" signal for orchestration and load balancers.

version.description: Semantic version of the running binary.

ImageRef.description: What an upload answers with: the new URL, so the client can show it without a round trip.

url.description: Same-origin URL of the stored image, versioned by its key.

ImportedPerson.description: One of the accounts an import brought over, as it stands now.

email.description: Empty when the archive carried none and nobody gave one: they cannot be invited by mail.

invited.description: Whether an invitation has already gone to that address.

InstanceCapabilities.description:
What a client can count on from this instance, before it has a session.

Today it carries one fact, and one that matters: whether the instance can send email. A sign-in
screen cannot guess it, and offering "we will email you a reset link" on an instance with no
relay sends someone to wait for a message that will never arrive. Running without a relay is a
supported configuration, not a misconfiguration, so the interface has to be able to say so.

api_version.description:
The major version of the API's paths: 1 for `/api/v1`, which only ever grows
(`docs/api-compatibility.md`).

email_delivery.description:
Whether an SMTP relay is configured. When false, every flow that would depend on a message
arriving has an alternative the interface offers instead.

features.description:
What this instance can do beyond every `/api/v1` instance, by name (`compat::FEATURES`): an
app checks for a name before using what it stands for, and does without when it is absent.

native_sessions.description:
Whether sign-in can hand a native app a session token (`session_delivery: "token"`), which
the iOS and Android apps need. Absent from an older instance, which the apps then ask to have
updated.

public_links.description: Whether files may be handed out by public link.

trash_retention_days.description: Days a removed file stays in the trash before it is erased (0: until the trash is emptied).

upload_max_bytes.description:
The largest file an upload accepts, in bytes, so the interface can turn a file down before
sending it rather than after.

version.description: The release this instance runs (`v1.2.3`), or `dev` outside a release build.

InstanceSettingsDto.description: The instance's settings, as an administrator sees and changes them.

show_instance_admins.description: Whether the interface tells everyone who administers the instance.

web_push_enabled.description: Whether the instance sends Web Push (see ADR 0001). Each person still opts in per browser.

InstanceSettingsPatch.description: A change to the instance's settings. Every field is optional: what is absent is left alone.

InvitationDto.description:
An outstanding invitation into a space, as listed to an administrator.

Deliberately carries no token: only its digest is stored, and the usable link is returned once,
at creation. A lost link is replaced by revoking this row and issuing another.

email.description: Address this invitation was addressed to; `None` for a shareable link.

invited_by.description: Display name of whoever issued it, when that account still exists.

status.description:
Why it is in that state: `active`, `accepted`, `revoked` or `expired`.

`usable` alone flattens four situations into one word, and the interface showed all of them
as "inactive" next to a Revoke button: an invitation someone had just accepted looked like a
failure that still needed cleaning up. An accepted invitation is a finished one.

usable.description: Whether it would be accepted right now: not revoked, not expired, uses left.

uses.description: How many times it has been accepted.

InvitationPreviewDto.description:
What someone holding an invitation token is told before they sign in.

Enough to decide whether to accept, and nothing more: never the member list, never whether the
address already has an account. Returned only for an invitation that is usable right now;
unknown, revoked, expired and exhausted tokens all get the same `404`, so the reason is never
disclosed.

email.description: Address the invitation is addressed to, so the screen can say which account to use.

invited_by.description: Display name of whoever issued it, when that account still exists.

InviteRequest.description: Who to write to. Source identifiers, as the archive spells them.

sent.description: How many emails the relay accepted.

skipped.description: Who was passed over, and why, in words meant for the administrator.

InviteeDto.description: Someone who may be invited, as the search offers them.

IssuedResetDto.description: A reset link, returned once and never retrievable again.

expires_in_secs.description: How long it stays valid, in seconds.

url.description: Absolute link for the account holder to open.

finished_at.description: When it ended, for an import the screen finds again rather than one it started itself.

LastMessageDto.description:
The latest message of a conversation, as a list of conversations shows it: the start of what was
said, who said it and when. A reply in a thread is not it: what a list previews is the
conversation itself. Nor, in a direct conversation, a system notice; a channel where nothing
was said since can preview one (it was created, an event was shared), but never somebody coming
or going, which is no news of the conversation.

author.description:
The author's display name ("Léa: ..."); for a notice, who did what it says. Absent when the
account is gone or the notice has nobody behind it.

excerpt.description:
The first characters of the body, raw markdown (the client flattens it for one line). For a
notice, its one detail (an event's title, a channel's new name), possibly empty.

mine.description: Whether the caller wrote it, so the list can say "You: ...".

system_event.description: Set when it is a notice rather than a message: what happened, which the client words.

LinkDto.description: One of a file's public links, for those who manage the file.

expired.description: Whether it has passed its expiry (it is then dead, and kept only to say so).

token.description: The key the public address carries: `/s/?t=<token>`.

LinkPreviewDto.description: A link preview, as the server read it from the page.

image_url.description: Same-origin address of the thumbnail of the site's preview image.

image_width.description: The original image's size, for the aspect ratio to reserve.

LinkableChannelDto.description: A channel an event may be linked to.

session_delivery.description:
How the session is handed over: the cookie (default, browsers) or the id itself (`token`,
native apps only; a browser asking for one is refused with `token_from_browser`).

MemberDto.description:
A space member row: identity plus the caller-independent role in the space. Presence is overlaid
client-side from the presence map, so it is not carried here.

avatar_url.description: Same-origin URL of the uploaded avatar; absent means the generated one.

role.description: Membership role in the space: `owner`, `admin`, `member` or `guest`.

title.description: Free-text job title / role label; `None` if unset.

MemberJoinedDto.description:
A member's arrival in a space, pushed in real time.

Carries the space it happened in, because a client holds one space on screen and ignores events
for the others, plus exactly the shape the member list already renders: the roster is patched
rather than refetched, which is also what keeps the mention and direct-message candidates live.

MemberLeftDto.description:
A member's departure from a space, pushed in real time.

The counterpart of [`MemberJoinedDto`], and carries only the two ids: an arrival has to describe
someone the recipient may never have seen, a departure names someone whose row is already on
screen and is only being taken off it.

MemberRoleChangedDto.description:
A membership whose role changed, returned by the call and pushed in real time.

A transfer produces two of these (the new owner and the former one), which is why the endpoint
answers with a list rather than with the one member it was addressed at: the caller has to be
able to draw both, and so does everyone watching.

MemberUpdatedDto.description:
A member's identity after a profile change, pushed in real time.

Carries no role: a profile is the same in every space, and the roles the recipient holds for
this person are already on screen. Every field is always serialised, `null` included, because
this is a replacement and not a patch: an absent `avatar_url` has to mean "the photo was
removed", which is indistinguishable from "unchanged" if the field is allowed to disappear.

MessageDto.description: A message as returned to clients, with its satellites folded in.

attachments.description: Files attached to the message, in attachment order.

author_id.description:
`None` for a system message about nothing in particular; a notice about someone (a join)
carries that person.

author_name.description:
Author display name, denormalized for direct rendering. Follows `author_id`, so a join notice
names the person who arrived and the client needs no second lookup.

body.description: Raw markdown (rendered client-side). Blank for a deleted tombstone.

deleted.description: Whether the message is a deleted tombstone.

oneOf.description:
For a calendar card, its event as the reader sees it now; absent when the event is gone or
no longer theirs to see (the body keeps its title).

imported.description: Whether the message was migrated from another tool.

last_reply_at.description:
When the thread was last answered (RFC 3339), for "last reply at 14:32" beside the count.
Absent for a message without replies.

oneOf.description:
The preview of the message's first link, read by the server (see `messaging::unfurl`).
Absent until it has been fetched, and for a message without a readable link.

parent_message_id.description: Parent message for a threaded reply; `None` for a root message.

pinned.description: Whether the message is pinned in its channel.

pinned_by.description:
Who pinned it, when it is pinned. Carried so a client can offer taking a pin down only to
the person who put it there (a moderator may take down anyone's, which it knows already).

reactions.description: Reaction buckets, sorted by first appearance.

reply_authors.description:
Display names of the last few people who answered in this thread, most recent first.

Denormalized on purpose: a feed draws a face next to "3 replies" without opening the thread,
and doing that from the client would cost one request per message on screen.

reply_count.description: Number of replies in this message's thread.

saved.description: Whether the caller saved (bookmarked) this message.

system_event.description: System-event discriminator for `system` messages (join/leave and similar).

MessagePage.description: A page of messages, newest-last, with an opaque cursor for the previous (older) page.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to fetch the next older page; `None` when the start was reached.

MfaCodeRequest.description: A second factor submitted with its pending MFA token (TOTP or recovery code).

MfaRequired.description:
Returned by login when the account requires a second factor. The client completes one of the
listed methods against `mfa_token` to obtain a session.

MfaStateResponse.description:
What second factors the caller's account actually holds.

The account screen had no way to ask this and so invented an answer, which is how it came to
report two-factor authentication as enabled on accounts that had never enrolled.

totp_enabled.description: A confirmed TOTP secret exists. An unconfirmed enrollment does not count.

Mode.description: How a session opens a file.

NativeCodeRequest.description: The app's challenge, for a native code: the SHA-256 of a verifier only the app holds, hex.

NativeExchangeRequest.description: A native code, and the verifier its challenge was made from.

NativeSession.description:
A session opened for a native app: the account, plus the id the app keeps in its keychain and
sends back as `Authorization: Bearer`.

NotificationDto.description: One in-app notification in the caller's inbox.

channel_name.description:
The channel's name, absent for a direct message.

Carried because a notification routinely arrives for a space the client has not loaded, and
a client cannot name a conversation it has never seen. Without it the only thing left to
show was the conversation's identifier, which is what a notification looked like whenever it
came from anywhere but the space on screen.

conversation_id.description: The conversation a message notification is about; absent for a reminder.

emoji.description: The emoji someone reacted with, for a `reaction`.

event_id.description:
A reminder's event and occurrence: what it is about and when it starts (RFC 3339 in UTC for
a timed event, `YYYY-MM-DD` for an all-day one).

event_my_status.description:
The recipient's answer to the event as it stands now, for an invitation kind they are on the
list of.

preview.description: A short plain-text excerpt of the source message; empty for a reminder.

read.description: Whether the caller has read the notification.

space_id.description:
The space it happened in. Carried so the inbox can be shown for the space on screen: without
it a client holding one space cannot tell which of its notifications belong there, and would
show a mention from another space in every space it opens. Absent for a reminder from a
personal calendar, which belongs to every space.

space_name.description:
The space's name, for the same reason: a notification says where it happened. Empty for a
reminder from a personal calendar.

NotificationPage.description: A page of notifications, newest first, with the caller's total unread count.

next_before.description: Cursor for the next (older) page, or `None` at the end.

NotificationPrefs.description:
A person's own notification settings.

Every field has a default, and a stored document missing a field (written before it existed)
takes that default rather than failing to load.

calendar_invitations.description:
Calendar invitations and what follows them (a change, a cancellation, a refusal), in the app
and by push, then by mail.

calendar_reminders.description:
Calendar reminders, in the app and by push, then by mail. Their own switches: a reminder is
asked for, not something that happened in a conversation.

email.description:
Email what is still unread after a while, when no Ruchoir page is open: the master switch
of the email fallback, then the same four kinds as above. `@channel` is off by default by
email: being one of a whole room is rarely worth a message in someone's inbox.

enabled.description: Master switch: off, nothing notifies, anywhere.

mentions.description:
What is signalled in the app and by push, per kind. `channel_mentions` is `@channel` and
`@here` (its name predates the others and is kept so stored documents still read).

messages.description:
A notification for every message, not only the ones addressed to the person: the default
for conversations left on `default` in spaces left on `default`. Off by default.

quiet_from.description:
Start of the quiet window, `HH:MM`, in the person's local time. May be later than
`quiet_to` for a window that runs past midnight.

quiet_hours.description: Hold notifications back during the window below.

quiet_to.description: End of the quiet window, `HH:MM`, local time.

reactions.description:
Someone reacted to one of my messages; a message I was told about was edited. In the app and
by push only: neither is ever worth an email.

sound.description: Play a sound with a notification.

utc_offset_minutes.description: Offset of the person's clock from UTC, in minutes (`+120` in Paris in summer).

busy.description:
A busy block from a calendar shared at the free/busy level: when, and nothing of what (no
title, place or notes), and it does not open.

description.description: The occurrence's notes: its own when it was changed apart, else the series'.

has_attendees.description: Whether anyone is invited to it.

invited.description: Whether the viewer sees it through an invitation alone (its calendar is not theirs to see).

my_reminders.description: The reminders the viewer gets for it, in minutes; empty when none.

my_status.description:
The viewer's answer for this occurrence (for the series, on an event): `needs_action`,
`accepted`, `tentative` or `declined`; `accepted` for the organiser of an event with
attendees; absent for anyone not on its list.

overridden.description: Whether this occurrence was changed apart from its series.

recurrence_id.description: Which occurrence of a series this is (its original start); absent for a one-off event.

start.description: RFC 3339 in UTC for a timed occurrence, `YYYY-MM-DD` for an all-day one.

OfficeCapabilities.description: What the client needs to know about live editing.

convert.description: Extensions the editor converts into an editable copy.

edit.description: Extensions the editor edits in place.

enabled.description: Whether the editor can be opened now (configured, and its discovery is known).

public_url.description: The editor's origin, which the client frames.

OidcProviders.description: Which optional OIDC connectors are enabled.

What an administrator changed about the people in an archive, after reading the plan and before
the run.

Held apart from the plan because it is not the archive's word: the archive says what its source
held, and this says what somebody decided about it. Carried on the job so a run resumed tomorrow
makes the same decisions as the one that started today.

The producer's own words, unchanged. Shown before the run, in full: summarising a declared
loss is another way of hiding it.

What replacing the instance would destroy, so the screen can show it next to what would
arrive. Counted on every plan, whether or not a replacement is asked for: an administrator
deciding between the two should see both halves at once.

warnings.description:
Problems the contract checks allow but an administrator should see, such as a reading
position naming a message that did not cross.

Accounts with no address at all. They arrive, they are placed, and they cannot be emailed:
the administrator has to give them an address or hand them a link.

the archive's history instead of being created beside it.

its first page), `video`, `audio` or `text`. Absent: nothing to show but its name.

tap, named as its list names it.

conversation_id.description: A message notification's conversation and message.

space_id.description: Absent for a reminder from a personal calendar.

delivered.description: How many of those the push services accepted the test for.

subscriptions.description: How many of the caller's browsers are subscribed.

ReactionDto.description: A reaction bucket on a message: the emoji, how many reacted, and whether the caller did.

mine.description: Whether the current caller is one of them (drives the toggle highlight).

users.description: Display names of the reactors, in first-reaction order (for the "who reacted" tooltip).

ReadCursorDto.description: One member's cursor, as `GET /conversations/{id}/read` returns it.

last_read_message_id.description: The last message this member has read; absent when they have read nothing here.

RecoveryCodesResponse.description: A freshly generated set of recovery codes, shown to the user exactly once.

RecoveryResetRequest.description: Reset a password with a recovery code instead of an emailed link.

invitation_token.description:
The invitation this registration came from, when it came from one.

An invitation addressed to this very address activates the account without the usual
confirmation round trip: it was delivered to that mailbox, which is the same proof a
verification email would collect. A shareable link proves nothing about the address and
therefore changes nothing here.

locale.description: The language to write to this account in, from the page they registered on.

instance_address.description:
The instance's own address, typed by hand. There is no instance name in the database, and
this is the one an administrator reads in their browser every day.

ResponseInput.description: An answer, for the series or for one date of it.

recurrence_id.description: One occurrence of a series; the whole series when absent.

restored_to_root.description: Its folder was gone, so it came back at the space root.

channel_name.description: The channel's name, absent for a direct message.

SavedMessageDto.description:
A bookmarked message, with where it was said.

The saved list is the caller's whole account, so most of it points at conversations the client
has not loaded and cannot name on its own.

SearchResults.description: Combined search results: matching messages and file names the caller can see.

SendMessageRequest.description: Post a new message (optionally as a threaded reply).

attachments.description:
Ids of already-uploaded files to attach (the caller must be able to read each, and each must
belong to the conversation's space).

config.description: Euro-Office's `docs_api_config`, a JSON string posted with the token.

is generated in the browser) and gives it to the editor.

url.description: The engine's address for this file, on the office hostname.

SetPresenceRequest.description: Set (or clear) the caller's manual presence override.

manual_presence.description: `active`, `away`, `dnd`, `invisible`, or `null`/absent to return to automatic presence.

ShareDto.description: One person a calendar is shared with.

SpaceDto.description:
A space the caller belongs to: the workspace-switcher entry and the bootstrap the SPA needs to
discover its channels (which are queried per space).

default_channel_id.description: The public channel every newly invited person joins.

icon_url.description: Same-origin URL of the uploaded icon; absent means the generated mark.

members.description: Total members in the space (drives the workspace member count in the UI).

mentions.description:
Unread notifications in this space (mention, thread reply, direct message): the things
addressed to the caller personally, and the only counter the rail shows as a number. A
notification for "every message" is not one of them: it says there is activity, which
`unread` already does.

notify_level.description:
How much this space notifies the caller: `default` (their own settings), `all`, `mentions`
or `none`.

role.description: The caller's role in the space: `owner`, `admin`, `member` or `guest`.

unread.description:
Unread root messages across the conversations the caller has joined in this space.

Drives the rail's discreet activity dot, deliberately not a number: one busy channel would
turn every space into a large figure that stops carrying information.

SpacePref.description: How much a whole space notifies the caller.

SpaceRefDto.description:
Where a slug leads: the space, and the slug it currently answers to.

Deliberately minimal. The caller already holds the space in its list; what it is missing is which
one an address from before a rename refers to, and what that address should now read as.

slug.description: The space's current slug, which may differ from the one that was looked up.

SpaceRemovedDto.description:
A space that stopped being the recipient's, pushed in real time.

`reason` separates the three ways that happens: they walked out (`left`), the space is gone for
everyone (`deleted`), or someone took them out of it (`removed`). The client drops it from the
rail in all three; what differs is what it says, and whether it says anything at all. A person
who left knows they left; a person who was removed has to be told, or a space simply vanishes
from under them.

SpaceUpdatedDto.description:
A space's shared identity after it changed, pushed in real time.

Deliberately not `SpaceDto`: that one carries the caller's role and their unread counters, which
are per-recipient and must never be broadcast. Same split as `ChannelSummaryDto`. Every field is
serialised, `null` included, for the reason `MemberUpdatedDto` gives: this replaces an identity
rather than patching one, so a removed icon has to be sayable.

SubscriptionKeys.description: A browser's subscription keys, as `PushSubscription.toJSON()` lays them out.

SubscriptionRequest.description: A browser's subscription, as `PushSubscription.toJSON()` lays it out.

TotpConfirm.description: A TOTP code submitted to confirm enrollment.

TotpEnrollResponse.description: TOTP enrollment material returned to the client to display.

otpauth_url.description: The `otpauth://` provisioning URI for manual entry.

qr_svg.description: An SVG QR code encoding the provisioning URI, ready to embed.

can_manage.description: Whether the caller may restore it or erase it.

original_folder_id.description: The folder it was in (absent: the space root).

original_folder_present.description: Whether that folder is still there: restoring lands at the root otherwise.

TypingRequest.description: A typing signal for a conversation (SSE-fallback clients POST this; WS clients send it inline).

UnlockRequest.description: The password, to unlock a protected link.

grant.description: The key the download and the thumbnail carry, for an hour.

UnsubscribeRequest.description: A subscription to forget, named by its endpoint.

UpcomingDto.description: An occurrence a channel lists as upcoming.

UpdateCalendar.description: A change to a calendar; absent fields stay as they are.

UpdateChannelRequest.description: Fields to change on a channel. An absent field is left untouched; an empty `topic` clears it.

allowed_roles.description:
Replace the roles the channel admits. An empty list lifts the restriction; absent leaves it
as it is, like every other field here.

type.description: `public`, `private` or `archived`. Moving to `archived` makes the channel read-only.

UpdateFileRequest.description:
Rename and/or move a file or folder. Renaming sets `name`; moving sets `parent_folder_id`, or
`move_to_root` to place the entry at the space root (distinct from "leave the parent unchanged").

UpdateMemberRoleRequest.description:
Change what a member is allowed to do in a space.

One of `owner`, `admin`, `member`, `guest`. Setting `owner` is a transfer rather than a
promotion: a space has one owner, so the one who hands it over becomes an `admin` in the same
write.

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Edit the caller's own profile. Absent fields are left unchanged; an empty string clears the field
(except `display_name`, which is required and ignored when blank).

locale.description: Interface language, so what the server writes arrives in the language the reader chose.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone (e.g. `Europe/Paris`), or blank to clear it.

The column existed and was read by the profile card from the start, and nothing could ever
write it: every profile reported a timezone nobody had chosen.

UpdateSpaceRequest.description: A change to a space's shared identity. Only the name for now.

name.description:
New display name. The slug is re-derived from it, and the one it replaces keeps resolving to
the same space, so the addresses people already hold keep arriving.

UserProfileDto.description:
A member's global profile, as shown in the profile card and member list. Presence is not folded
in here: it is volatile and sourced separately (`GET /spaces/{id}/presence` and realtime events),
so this stays the stable, self-editable profile. Returned only for a user who shares a space with
the caller.

avatar_url.description:
Same-origin URL of the uploaded avatar. Absent means there is none, and the client generates
one from the display name, which is what it already does by default.

is_bot.description: Whether this is a service account (e.g. the import assistant).

is_instance_admin.description:
Whether this person administers the instance.

Not a privacy leak but the point: recovering an account that has lost both its password and
its recovery codes means asking an administrator, and nobody can ask someone they cannot
identify. It says nothing about what the account can see, only who to go to.

locale.description:
Interface language (`fr`, `en`, ...), or absent when they have not chosen one.

On the profile for the same reason the timezone is: it says something about working with
this person. Nothing else reads it, and it is the language *they* read, not one to write to
them in from the interface.

timezone.description: IANA timezone (e.g. "Europe/Paris"); the client derives the local time from it.

title.description: Free-text job title / role label (e.g. "Gérante"); `None` if unset.

UserSummary.description: Public view of an account returned to the client. Never includes secrets.

active.description:
Whether the account can sign in already. False after an ordinary registration, which waits on
the address being confirmed; true when an invitation had already proved the address.

is_instance_admin.description:
Whether this account administers the instance. Carried so the client knows whether to offer
the account-recovery screen; the routes behind it check the flag themselves.

manual_presence.description:
The caller's own availability choice (`away`, `dnd`, `invisible`), or absent for automatic.

Only ever sent to the account it belongs to. It is a choice, not a state: what other people
see is the presence computed from it and from a live connection, which is carried by the
presence endpoints. The client needs it to show which entry of its availability menu is the
one in force, and it has no other way to know.

timezone.description:
The account's timezone, or absent when it has none.

Carried on the session so the client can notice an account that has never had one and offer
the browser's, which is a fact about where this person is rather than a guess. Without it
the profile card had a "local time" row that nobody could ever fill.

current.description: The version the file serves now.

ViewEntryDto.description: One entry of a view: the file, where it lives, and for "shared with me" who sent it where.

path.description: Its folders from the space root down (empty at the root, and for a private conversation's file).

shared_in_name.description: The channel's name (a direct message has none to give).

WebRedeemRequest.description: A web handoff code, redeemed by the page the app opened.

last_backup.description: When the last backup was recorded, if ever. A replacement is refused without a recent one.

post.description:
The recovery code *is* the proof of possession: it was shown once, noted by its owner, and is
good for a single use. Minting an intermediate reset token from it would add a round trip and
nothing else, so the new password is set in the same request.

Every failure answers the same way, whether the address is unknown, the account has no password,
or the code is wrong: the caller learns only that it did not work. Failures feed the same
per-address cooldown as sign-in, because a guessing endpoint without one would be the weakest
door into the instance even with codes this long.

post.description:
The ordinary case creates an account, unverified, and sends a confirmation; no session opens
until the address is confirmed.

The other case is an account that already exists and has never been used: an import places
people in their spaces and channels before any of them has signed in, so the account, its
membership and its history are all here, waiting. Registering with the invitation addressed to
that person **claims** that account rather than colliding with it. Anything else about an
existing address is still a conflict.

answers are counted per account and spend the code (see [`tokens::CODE_TRIES`]); the per-IP rate
limit applies on top.

Joining is something you do to yourself (`PUT .../membership`); this is the other half, and it
did not exist. The dialog offering it showed every member of the space with a checkbox, added
nobody, and reported success, which also made it look as though unchecking someone would remove
them. Removing is a third thing, with its own authorization, and is not this endpoint either.

Anyone who is in the channel may bring someone else in, as in every tool people arrive here
from; a moderator of the space may do it without being in the channel themselves. Targets must
already belong to the space: a channel is not a way into one.

The same rule as a space role, on the channel's own shorter ladder (`member` < `admin` <
`owner`): act only on someone strictly below you, hand out only a rank strictly below your own.

nobody changes their own role. A space owner or administrator counts as the channel's owner here,
because they may already archive it and delete anyone's message in it: being able to moderate a
channel but not to say who else may would be a line drawn nowhere.

opened the room, the space's administrators can moderate it regardless, and a channel left with

patch.description:
**One rule, applied twice.** You may only act on someone ranked strictly below you, and you may
only hand out a rank strictly below your own. Ranks are `guest` < `member` < `admin` < `owner`.
Everything follows from it: nobody can change their own role, an admin can make members and
guests but not other admins, an admin cannot demote another admin, and nobody outranks the owner.

**The one exception is the transfer.** An owner may set someone else to `owner`, and becomes an
`admin` in the same write. A space therefore has exactly one owner at any moment, which is what
the refusal in [`leave_space`] points at: an owner who wants out hands the space over first. The
demotion is not a courtesy the code invents, it is the transfer: two people holding the same
space would make "the last owner" a question rather than a fact.

Invitations cannot grant `owner` either (the schema constrains them to `admin`, `member`,
`guest`), so this endpoint is the only door ownership ever moves through after a space is
created.

delete.description:
Only the caller's own membership goes, here and in the channels of that space. What they wrote
stays: a channel is a shared record, and taking one member's messages out of it would rewrite
everyone else's history. Coming back needs a new invitation, which is what makes this worth a
confirmation on the way out rather than an undo afterwards.

**The last owner is refused.** An owner may walk out of a space that still has another owner;
the last one cannot, because the space would be left with nobody able to administer it, invite
into it or delete it. They are told to hand ownership over or to delete the space, which is a
`409`: the request is not malformed, the space is simply not in a state that allows it.
